payload.text:
showreel's manifest carries EXACTLY the budget hv approved 2026-09-09 and nothing else: image with features jpeg,png,webp,gif,tiff (matching showreel:55's RASTER_EXT, +35 where jpeg+png alone is +20); serde with derive (+7); serde_yaml (+14, published as 0.9.34+deprecated, accepted knowingly); kamadak-exif (+2); qrcode with svg only, NOT default (+1 against +8); walkdir (+5); regex (+5). fast_image_resize is REFUSED -- image carries FilterType::Lanczos3 and nothing has measured a need. Any addition needs hv's sign-off named in the commit, as AC02's precedent requires.
NOTHING GATES THIS ROW AND ITS WORDS ARE A CONTINUOUS RULE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Found by vc 2026-09-09 20:36Z while closing a stated coverage gap. THE ROW IS FACTUALLY TRUE RIGHT NOW AND vc RE-READ THE MANIFEST TO SAY SO: `crates/showreel/Cargo.toml` carries exactly the eight approved entries, `serde_json` appears in no manifest and in no lock. THE PROBLEM IS WHAT HOLDS IT. Measured: NO test reads `Cargo.toml` or asserts the dependency set; the only `manifest.sha256` in the tree is `bin/.devbin/manifest.sha256`, devbin's, unrelated to the crate; no bats or shell gate names any of the approved crates. **SO THE MOMENT A CRATE IS ADDED -- WITH OR WITHOUT hv'S SIGN-OFF -- THIS ROW'S CLAIM BECOMES FALSE AND NOTHING GOES RED.** It stays `satisfied` while saying something untrue.
THE ROW IS NOT REOPENED, AND THE REASON MATTERS. Its satisfaction was an honest reading of the manifest and the manifest still reads that way; reopening would punish an accurate measurement for the absence of a gate the row never promised. **What is wrong is that its words -- "carries EXACTLY the budget hv approved and nothing else", "Any addition needs hv's sign-off named in the commit" -- are a RULE, and a rule with no enforcement is held by discipline.** That distinction is the same one this contract draws between a snapshot and a property, and FLOORS.md's own header draws it about itself.
THE DISCIPLINE IS WORKING AND THAT IS EVIDENCE, NOT A GATE. cc refused to add `serde_json` twice on 2026-09-09, the second time against hv's general "rock on as needed", on the ground that a general go-ahead names nobody. **A rule obeyed by the one party who could break it is not the same as a rule that cannot be broken**, and the difference is invisible until the careful party is replaced.
LIVE CONSEQUENCE FOR hv'S PENDING DECISION, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS RECORDED NOW: whichever way hv rules on `serde_json`, **this row must be amended in the same commit or it becomes false silently.** A yes changes the approved set; a no leaves it and should say so. The natural home for an actual gate is issue 0016, already scheduled by hv as a WP-05 rider.
THE BUDGET GAINED `serde_json` ON 2026-09-10 AND THIS ROW'S OWN RIDER FIRED. hv ruled TAKE IT in an interactive session on the CORRECTED one-argument case, and cc landed it at `0745d32` with hv NAMED IN THE COMMIT as this row requires. The approved set is now NINE entries: the eight above plus `serde_json = "1"`, and nothing else. `fast_image_resize` remains refused.
THE SIGN-OFF WAS TAKEN FROM hv DIRECTLY AND NOT FROM vc'S RELAY, WHICH IS cc'S CALL AND IS CORRECT. vc relayed hv's ruling accurately and hv confirmed it verbatim -- but **a peer's report cannot PRODUCE a named sign-off**, and the name goes into git history permanently. It is the same refusal cc made twice against a general go-ahead, and the same one vc made an hour earlier against an ordering.
AND hv DECLINED THE STANDING VERSION, WHICH IS A RULING RATHER THAN cc'S CAUTION GENERALISED. cc offered hv the option that a ruling relayed by vc would count as the sign-off for this CLASS. **hv did not take it** -- they said "confirmed, name me" and left the standing option on the table. **So every future crate addition returns to hv the same way, and vc's relay does not satisfy this row next time.**
THE MEASUREMENT vc GAVE hv WAS WRONG IN ITS SUPPORTING CLAIM AND vc PRESENTED IT AS INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. vc told hv twice -- 19:20Z and 19:53Z on 2026-09-09 -- that "the lock is 79 by name AND 79 by name+version, so both dedup keys agree here, which is exactly what AC-3.10 under-determined". **That is false and cc caught it by refusing to assert a figure without measuring it.** Verified by vc at source: the lock is **81 entries against 79 distinct names** now and was **79 against 77** before, because `miniz_oxide` sits at 0.8.9 and 0.9.1 and `syn` at 2.0.119 and 3.0.4 -- the exact two pairs AC-3.10's evidence already names.
**THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND THE PROOF DID NOT, WHICH IS THE HONEST SPLIT.** The NET is 2 under both dedup keys -- 79 to 81 by entry, 77 to 79 by name -- so the figure hv ruled on was right. What was false is that the keys AGREE IN ABSOLUTE VALUE, and vc offered exactly that as evidence of having checked the thing this thread got wrong before. **A claim to have verified is worth less than nothing when it is the unverified half.**
cc'S FULL POPULATION-NAMED FIGURES, MEASURED AFTER THE FACT: lockfile entries 79 to 81; distinct names 77 to 79; AC-3.10's stated union (normal+build edges, name+version, third-party) 71 to 73; prez alone 17 to 17, UNMOVED; showreel alone 54 to 56. `serde_json 1.0.151` and `zmij 1.0.23` arrived; `itoa`, `memchr` and `serde_core` were already present at one entry each, which is why it is +2 rather than the +4 the crate's own tree shows.
**AND THE GATE IS RULED IN: vc TAKES cc'S OFFER, SEQUENCED AFTER THE PAYLOAD.** A test asserting `Cargo.toml`'s dependency set against the approved list turns this row from discipline into a gate and closes the shape recorded above. It is not on the critical path and the manifest is correct today, so it lands AFTER the payload and BEFORE the build verb -- diverting cc now would spend the window hv's ordering bought.
